title: KV pool island reclamation and seamless consolidation strategy
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: GPU memory fragmentation in the KV cache is driving elevated per-token costs and occasional tail latency spikes during continuous batching. Small, long-lived allocations ("islands") combined with opportunistic large writes lead to underutilized pockets that block new KV slots and force violent eviction/migration paths.

Goal: Design and ship an Island Reclamation + Seamless Consolidation playbook that reduces fragmentation by opportunistically merging underutilized slots, amortizing migrations across low-utilization micro-epochs, and integrating with continuous-batching policies to avoid throughput regressions. The solution must be safe for live serving (no global pauses), observable, and provide knobs for conservative/aggressive modes.

Key ideas:
- Island detection via a heatmap derived from access recency and per-slot occupancy metrics (hotness score, allocation age, occupancy ratio).
- Lightweight tombstones and slot-forwarding pointers to permit in-place remapping of KV handles without invalidating in-flight batched requests.
- Micro-defrag epochs: schedule consolidation during low-traffic windows (per-GPU sliding windows) and coordinate with the batching controller to temporarily drain long-lived KV prefetches.
- Amortized relocation: break migrations into tiny increments (micro-moves) tied to background worker budget and burst capacity, reducing tail latency.
- Opportunistic coalescing: merge adjacent free fragments into larger runs using a compacting pass when contiguous free space reaches threshold, enabling placement of larger KV entries and reducing cross-slab scattering.
- Pointer indirection layer: maintain a small indirection table per-GPU that maps logical KV indices to physical slot addresses to make forwarding cheap and localized. Indirection table is sharded and kept small to avoid additional memory pressure.
- Integration with continuous batching: the scheduler will avoid relocating slots referenced by current batch windows and will notify the batch controller to postpone large batches that would exacerbate eviction churn.
- Telemetry and SLOs: add fragmentation_ratio, island_count, average_relocation_size, and relocation_throughput metrics. Expose anomaly alerts when fragmentation_ratio > 0.35 or relocation_throughput exceeds budget.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Indirection adds a small lookup cost per KV access; we evaluate whether a 1-2% CPU increase is acceptable given memory wins.
- Aggressive consolidation reduces fragmentation faster but can increase transient network/GPU bandwidth due to relocations. We provide conservative defaults and an aggressive config for Dedicated customers.
- We avoid any solution requiring global stop-the-world compaction. All work must be incremental and bounded.

Success criteria:
- 25-40% reduction in fragmentation_ratio on synthetic heavy-churn workloads within 24 hours of deployment.
- No >5% regression in 99th-percentile request latency during background consolidation for P95 workloads.
- Clear cost-per-token reduction observed on benchmark suite (>=10% improvement for long-context, high-churn workloads).

Deliverables:
- Design doc and simulation harness for island detection thresholds and amortized relocation scheduling.
- Runtime changes: indirection table, tombstone/forwarding mechanisms, micro-defrag worker, batch coordinator hooks.
- Telemetry dashboards and alerting rules.
- Canary rollout plan: start in private deployments with conservative mode, then Dedicated, then hosted with opt-in.

Open questions:
1) Indirection table size vs. lookup latency: how many bits per entry can we afford before CPU overhead becomes material?
2) When to trigger a compaction pass vs. relying on micro-moves for long-lived islands?
3) Best heuristics for coordinating with the continuous-batcher to minimize tail effects?
comments: 2026-02-12 - Maya Chen: Initial product ask from infra showed repeated eviction thrash on long-context chat workloads. Created spike to quantify island sizes using existing KV telemetry.

2026-02-18 - Owen Patel: Prototype heatmap generator running on dev cluster. Early results show 3 distinct island shapes: narrow high-age islands, wide low-occupancy islands, and interleaved pockets. Posting sample heatmap to design doc.

2026-02-25 - Design review (Priya Rao): Suggested pointer indirection instead of relocating handles that are referenced by external pointers; flagged indirection table size as a risk. Action: run microbench for indirection lookup overhead.

2026-03-02 - Benchmark update (Owen Patel): Amortized micro-move approach reduced 99p latency spikes by ~30% in pump-test. Relocation bandwidth stayed under 8% of GPU memory bandwidth with conservative config.
2026-03-08 - Security review (Anita Gomez): No sensitive data flows added; recommend marking telemetry endpoints with RBAC and rate limits. Security review not required but follow recommendations.

2026-03-11 - QA note (Jared Lee): Stress test with continuous-batching synthetic workload exposed a corner case where forwarded pointers race with prefetch reads. Added a short-lived epoch fence to prevent races; requires further stabilization.

2026-03-12 - PM alignment (Lina Torres): PMs asked for canary plan and rollback thresholds. Added release gate: fragmentation_ratio improvement observed for 48h on canary, no regressions in 99p latency.
